newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may raise sugar export tax exemption soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may raise sugar export tax exemption soon.

text.p: Brazil's Ministry of Industry and Commerce may raise as early as next week the sugar export limit exempted from tax, a senior commodities official said.
Pedro Cabral, head of the sugar and alcohol department, said officials were completing studies to exempt from export tax the 20 percent of the sugar export quota that has not yet been made tax-free.
"We want to do it as quickly as possible to meet demands from producers," he told Reuters, adding that "in principle" it could happen next week.
The government set exports at 5.2 million tonnes of sugar in its 1996/97 crop plan but only exempted an initial 4.2 million tonnes from tax.
Liberating the remaining 1.0 million tonnes was left to a later date to give the ministry an opportunity to monitor the harvest and in particular the supply of alcohol.
"Production is going well and the supply of alcohol to the domestic market is above target," Cabral said.
He denied that the ministry had already prepared a decree authorizing the increase in export tax exemptions.
